report.question: When a stage captures a screenshot, a window handle, a clipboard value or an accessibility tree, does it capture only the intended surface - and what happens when the intended window is occluded or not focused?
report.answer:
NO for the Windows screenshot rail, and the failure is silent and total. take_screenshot.ps1 uses the window handle ONLY to compute a rectangle (GetWindowRect, line 138) and then reads that rectangle off the desktop compositor (CopyFromScreen, line 156), so the window's IDENTITY never reaches the pixel read. Measured against a synthetic target: unoccluded 1.00 target; 50% occluded 0.50 target / 0.50 foreign; fully occluded 0.00 target / 1.00 foreign - the real repo script, invoked exactly as documented with -WindowHandle, returned an image containing none of the requested window and all of an unrelated one, with exit code 0 and no warning. Focus is irrelevant: the target was unfocused in both failing states, and the window-scoped PrintWindow alternative returned 1.00 target in every state, so the defect is a missing capture-API flag, not an OS limitation. PrintWindow appears ZERO times in 7,120 scanned files (matcher proven live), so no window-scoped path exists anywhere on the Windows rail. Browser-mediated capture (55 page.screenshot sites, 14 a11y-snapshot sites) is renderer-scoped and structurally immune, though not executed under occlusion here. The clipboard rail reads a globally shared buffer guarded only by ContainsImage(). On storage: nothing outside the target surface is prevented from being stored, nothing is reaped (845 PNGs / 94,183,329 B / 837.1 days in the documented default destination), and the destination grants two Codex sandbox service accounts ReadAndExecute over the whole archive.

SECOND-INSTANCE VERIFICATION (independent re-derivation, 2026-08-12). Every load-bearing claim above was re-measured by a second instance that did not reuse the first instance's harness. (1) A fresh live occlusion experiment with different marker colours, different geometry and a different driver reproduced the leak exactly: 0.0000 target / 1.0000 foreign under full occlusion, 1.0000 target on the unoccluded control. (2) All seven stored frames re-decoded with Pillow/libpng+numpy match the original PowerShell GDI+ histogram to four decimal places. (3) The retention figures reproduce EXACTLY under a second enumerator (os.scandir vs Get-ChildItem), and .playwright-mcp grew 283->290 files in four hours, which strengthens rather than weakens the unbounded-retention finding. (4) Two independent ACL readers (Win32 GetFileSecurity and icacls.exe) agree, and the orphaned-SID detector was proven silent on a clean control directory. (5) The cross-vendor refuter's single PARTIAL was upheld as a real harness defect but shown not to invalidate the measurement it qualifies, because an unpainted bitmap is black and the frames have zero black pixels.

The sharpest new datum is unplanned: attempt 1 of the second instance had NO visibility interlock, the OS refused its window-activation call, and the repo script then wrote two images of the owner's real desktop -- unrelated applications -- while being asked for a specific window handle, with exit code 0 and no warning. Those frames were destroyed immediately. That is the estate precedent reproducing itself, live, inside the audit of itself, and it raises the practical severity of D1: the failure does not require an adversary or an unusual desktop, only a capture issued while the requested window is not on top -- the normal condition for an automated agent that cannot take the foreground.

It is recorded because it is the strongest digest a self-describing file CAN carry, and unlike the sibling receipts' values it is exactly recomputable by a third party. The reducer will still report condition 3 as a mismatch; that is disclosed, not suppressed.
